Specify -std=c99 compiler flag for Cython files.

PyTorch's build_ext subclass automatically adds -std=c++14 to everything,
disregarding whether it's a C or C++ file. Clang throws an error with this
flag (gcc only prints a warning).
To work-around PyTorch's behavior we can specify a correct -std flag for
Cython files (-std=c99 is good hopefully?).

Merge pull request #10 from FalkonML/ci-incore

v0.6 -- InCoreFalkon, CUDA LAUUM, Bug fixes

The driving change was the implementation of an in-core version of Falkon, suitable for smaller data analyses. Here the data is always kept inside the GPU, thus the model can train much faster. The result is the InCoreFalkon class.

LAUUM was improved to use a CUDA implementation for the inner-loop function.

API changes are limited to the `FalkonOptions` class, where certain option names have changed.

Several bug fixes were also introduced, and edge-cases fixed.

message:
Ensure storage_offset is int

Older versions of PyTorch complain if storage_offset is e.g. a np.int64
object (which it will be in certain cases, since it is the return value
of a np.prod call). We cast to int to make sure this is not a problem.

This should be done for size, stride and probably other arguments as well,
but since it's not a problem on newer PyTorch versions we keep things as
they are, since those are usually not np.int64.

author: gmeanti <giacomo.meanti@gmail.com>
message:
Falkonv7.1

Hyperparameter optimization (falkon_hopt module) and a big refactoring.

The most significant changes are:
 - Consolidated C/CUDA extensions in the csrc directory. This
   helps with compilation time, and package size.
 - Consolidated the fMM, fMMv APIs to avoid having to deal with
   separate CPU, CUDA imlementations. There is still some work
   to do here for the batch APIs.
 - Changed the kernel API to allow for differentiable kernel
   computations. This was necessary to implement the hyperparameter
   optimization module.
 - Added falkon_hopt module for hyperparameter optimization (gradient
   based) with several different objective functions.
 - Some work done on the CI side, but still partial/not working.

message:
Take adjoint of `Q` rather than transpose

This came up in a nanosoldier run in https://github.com/JuliaLang/julia/pull/46196. Transposes of Q's don't have specialized functions and fall back to `AbstractMatrix` methods, in particular in multiplication. Generic multiplication, however, is defined in terms of elementwise `getindex`, which is expensive and very slow in contrast to dense or structured matrices.

* Introduce an approximate Hessian and a new `get_hessian!` function.
* unify cost/gradient/hessian signature.
* increase test coverage.

message:
Rework high level interfaces (#392)

* trigger all ambiguity errors.
* Move dispatch on p into subfunctions, that existed before anyways.
* rework the safeguards to dispatch internally.
* remove deprecated definitions.
* remove all deprecated parameters.
* rename set_manopt_parameter! to set_parameter and get_manopt_parameter to get_parameter
* unify stabilisation through projection keyword.
* remove `update_stopping_criterion` to update values in the stopping criterion and submerge it in the set_parameter! scheme
* unify state constructors of ALM and ARC
* Adapt EPM.
* Finish DoC and DCPPA
* Unify how p and X are passed to states overall in all states.
* Sketch a first idea of a factory.
* Fix scaling parameter in quasi newton. This resolvs #382
* Start changing the docs snippets to using a documentation glossary
* 📚Finish the glossary work
* Unify signatures, fix a few tex typos and improve english on the factory info/note.

message:
Take adjoint of `Q` rather than transpose (#142)

This came up in a nanosoldier run in https://github.com/JuliaLang/julia/pull/46196. Transposes of Q's don't have specialized functions and fall back to `AbstractMatrix` methods, in particular in multiplication. Generic multiplication, however, is defined in terms of elementwise `getindex`, which is expensive and very slow in contrast to dense or structured matrices.

message:
fix(get-file-list): correct logic to handle different scenarios

Scenario 1:

Function is called from the directory where the "rootfile" lives.
This is simple, as all the files will have includes relative to this
directory. However, we do need to handle recursion because models and
includes can be split into any numbers of folders/levels.

Scenario 2:

Function is not called from the directory where the "rootfile" lives.
The directory is specified as the "rootdir". Here, we need to append the
rootdir to all the includes also so that they can be correctly found.

This case is not suggested, especially for archiving.

author: Ankur Sinha (Ankur Sinha Gmail) <sanjay.ankur@gmail.com>
message:
feat(vispy-plotter): implement heuristic to ensure performance

We implement a heuristic based on a `precision` tuple. This takes two
parameters:

- the number of decimals that should be used to group segments into
  meshes
- the total number of meshes to limit the visualization to.

In general, more meshes means more detail, but less performance. Here,
the user can provide what precision they want to use. The method
includes a heuristic where it will reduce precision until the number of
meshes being used is less than the provided threshold value.

author: Ankur Sinha (Ankur Sinha Gmail) <sanjay.ankur@gmail.com>
message:
fix(file-list): correct recursive file listing

When there are models that follow a recursive structure. For example:

```
something.net.nml -> ./cells/cell.nml -> ./channels/channel.nml
```

When processing the cell.nml file, we must do it relative to its
location, not relative to the root file (something.net.nml) so that the
paths are correct in the final list of files included in the model.

We do this by making sure that when recursing through the list, we pass
the location of the "new" rootfile, and when we append the processed
file to the file list, we include its "rootdir", which would be relevant
to the "main" rootfile.

message:
refactor(plotting): split out on-demand loading to separate function

The logic here is that if a user provides us a file to plot, we don't
need to load all the includes in the file and so on.  We can load only
the information we need to plot the morphology plots and disregard the
other information.

However, if a loaded model is given, we just use that---it's already in
memory, and there's no point of copying it to remove things, since
that'll just use even more memory.

This is required because all the arguments of functions that use caching
must be hashable. Now, the user should see the required type for the
`axes_pos` argument is a tuple, but if they miss that and provide a
list, they'll get a `not hashable` error, which isn't the most clear.

So, we help the user out by casting a list into a tuple where possible.

author: Ankur Sinha (Ankur Sinha Gmail) <sanjay.ankur@gmail.com>
message:
feat(vispy-3d-detailed): take advantage of lru_cache

We make the function arguments all hashable so that we can use the
lru_cache here also. For most networks, there will be one cell object
that is placed at different locations in the population by specifying an
offset. The mesh creator takes the offset into account, but other than
that, it is not used. So, we don't need to pass it to our cell specific
method. For all cells of the same type for the population, we only
process the first one, and the rest of the meshes are taken from the
cache. We then add the offset for each cell instance to the mesh data
before passing it to the mesh creator.

So, for 100 cells of the same type, we only process the one cell.
The other 99 are picked from the cache.

For the moment, I've set the lru size to 100. I don't think we'll come
across networks that use more than 100 cells anytime soon.

Note that this does not help for cases where the same cell has also been
rotated because for each of these cells, NeuroML requires a new
population. There, we must process each cell individually, for each
population.

amend jitclass import from numba in Cellpose notebook

Hi,

I updated the numba imports for section 6.2 (3D predictions) because jitclass needs to be imported from numba.experimental otherwise we get the error message below:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
ImportError                               Traceback (most recent call last)
<ipython-input-3-0fa970c2ce00> in <module>
----> 1 from numba import jitclass, float64
      2 from numba import jit

ImportError: cannot import name 'jitclass' from 'numba' (/usr/local/lib/python3.7/dist-packages/numba/__init__.py)
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Also, the Anisotropy explanation says that the default value is 1 but by default the value was set to 2, so I set it to 1.

Thanks a lot
=)

author: aminrezaei-img <85622799+aminrezaei-img@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
Update EmbedSeg_2D_ZeroCostDL4Mic.ipynb

Uninstalling the incompatible decencies and re-installing tested versions that met the dependency requirement solved PyPI related issues. 

After reviewing the EmbedSeg PyPI release history and comparing its source code with the EmbedSeg GitHub repo, I noticed a number of changes, of which all resulted in our version of notebook to not run properly. 

So in the section relating to installing key dependencies, I did change the path that PIP retrieves EmbedSeg. From here on forward, we are installing EmbedSeg from its GitHub repo (which is by far the most updated version) 

%pip install git+https://github.com/juglab/EmbedSeg.git

Another point to consider was a minor change in the original train section of EmbedSeg. The variable normalization_factor in train_dataset_dict and val_dataset_dict are no longer needed on the updated EmbedSeg version, hence the two are muted. 

After implementing these changes and running the notebook, I did not encounter any issues.

author: esgomezm <43643518+esgomezm@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
Export 2D UNet to DeepImageJ format

Major changes:
- Add an appendix at the end of the notebook to export the trained model to DeepImageJ bundled model format. It creates a new folder called "deepimagej" inside the model folder. "deepimagej" contains all the files needed for its execution/test in Fiji and is compatible with DeepImageJ version 1.0.1, i.e. the configuration file is in XML format.
- The resulting image in DeepImageJ is slightly different. Two are the reasons:
    · DeepImageJ takes into account the halo of the model (receptive field of the pixel).
    · Percentile Normalization: it may vary slightly from ImageJ and Python. See the macro code here: https://github.com/deepimagej/imagej-macros/blob/master/PercentileNormalization.ijm

Minor changes:
- To follow the same logic as when the trained model is saved, the function 'saveResult' now creates the directory 'save_path' if it does not exist. It affects uniquely to the results folder that was not created by default.

message:
Test: Verify constrained triangle collection after vertex addition

This commit introduces a new test case, TriangleCollectorPostConstraintSplitTest.java,
to verify the correct identification of constrained triangles after a new vertex
is added to the boundary of an existing polygon constraint, causing an edge split.

Analysis of the issue regarding the failure to identify such triangles
revealed that the current constraint propagation logic within
EdgePool.splitEdge appears to correctly handle the updating of flags and
constraint map entries for newly created edge segments. The new test case
passes with the existing codebase, confirming this behavior for the tested
scenario.

This test will serve as a regression test to ensure this behavior is
maintained. No code changes to the library were made as part of this issue's
resolution, as the existing mechanisms seem to cover the reported scenario.

fix: Correct MockEdge implementation in unit tests

Updates the MockEdge static inner class in SegmentUtilityTest.java and
TriangleUtilityTest.java to fully and correctly implement the
IQuadEdge interface.

Key changes:
- Ensured all methods from IQuadEdge are present with correct signatures.
- Removed methods from MockEdge that are not part of the IQuadEdge interface (e.g., getDx, getDy, getVertex(int)).
- Corrected the signature of setConstrained to setConstrained(int constraintIndex), removing any boolean versions.
- For TriangleUtilityTest.java's MockEdge, ensured 'forward' and 'reverse' fields and setters are present to support testing the SimpleTriangle constructor. These are initialized to 'this' in the MockEdge constructor to prevent NPEs if not explicitly set.

These changes address compilation errors caused by an incomplete or incorrect MockEdge implementation that did not align with the IQuadEdge interface.

message:
feat: Introduce Delaunay Refinement (Ruppert's Algorithm)

Adds support for Delaunay mesh refinement using Ruppert's algorithm.
This feature aims to improve the quality of triangles in a Triangulated
Irregular Network (TIN) by iteratively inserting points.

Key components of this change:

1.  **`RuppertsRefiner.java`** (in `org.tinfour.refinement`):
    *   The main class that orchestrates the refinement process.
    *   It takes an `IIncrementalTin` and quality criteria (minimum angle
        and/or maximum circumradius-to-shortest-edge ratio).
    *   The refinement loop identifies "poor-quality" triangles and
        "encroached" segments (constrained edges whose diametral circles
        are pierced by other TIN vertices or by circumcenters of
        poor-quality triangles).
    *   Poor-quality triangles have their circumcenters inserted, unless
        doing so would encroach a segment; in that case, the segment
        is split.
    *   Encroached segments are split by inserting their midpoints.
    *   The process continues until no poor-quality triangles or
        encroached segments remain according to the criteria.

2.  **Utility Classes** (in `org.tinfour.utils`):
    *   **`TriangleUtility.java`**: Provides helper methods for triangle
        calculations, such as computing angles, finding the shortest
        edge, calculating the circumradius-to-shortest-edge ratio,
        and determining if a triangle meets the quality criteria.
    *   **`SegmentUtility.java`**: Provides helper methods for segment
        (edge) calculations, including computing a segment's
        diametral circle and checking if a point encroaches upon
        a segment.
    *   **`Circle.java`**: A simple class to represent a circle, used
        for diametral circle calculations.

3.  **Testing:**
    *   JUnit tests were added for `TriangleUtility`, `SegmentUtility`,
        `Circle`, and `RuppertsRefiner`.
    *   Tests cover various scenarios, including valid inputs, edge cases,
        degenerate conditions, and the different logic paths within the
        refinement algorithm.

4.  **Documentation:**
    *   Javadoc comments were added to all new public classes, methods,
        and constructors to explain their purpose, parameters, and behavior.

The current implementation of `RuppertsRefiner` uses a straightforward
approach where the queue of items to process is fully refreshed after
each modification to the TIN. While correct, this may not be the most
performant solution for very large TINs or complex refinement scenarios.
Future optimizations could focus on more localized updates to the queue.

message:
merge adaptive smc and adaptive distance smc update functions

in smc:

1. separated adaptive_threshold and adaptive_quantile functionalities. adaptive_threshold now means that thresholds are not predetermined vs adaptive_quantile means that the adaptive thresholds are estimated based on adaptive quantiles determined based on density ratio estimation. this was needed because adaptive distance smc does not have predetermined threshold but also does not use quantile adaptation.

removed the separate update function

author: Ulpu Remes <ulpu.remes@pm.me>
message:
fix nested acceptance

about nested acceptance: rejection sampler sorts samples based on distance and assumes that the n_samples first samples are the accepted sample. however when several distance functions and and thresholds are used as acceptance criterion, the smallest samples selected based on any one distance measure could contain samples that are not acceptable based on another distance measure and associated threshold.

about what was fixed: previous version checked whether a new batch contains samples where one or more distance measure is not below threshold and substituted all distances in such samples with infinities. this would ensure that the samples would not be sorted as smallest ones when the batch is merged with previous samples. however based on travis, the distances that were overwritten are a read-only variable in linux. hence this new version does not overwrite the distances but checks whether there are acceptable samples in a batch and if so, merges these with the previous samples.

author: uremes <uremes@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
Add adaptive distance SMC-ABC (#346)

* add adaptive distance SMC

note: uses standard rejection sampler

* add adaptive distance node

added new class and updated adaptive distance SMC to use the adaptive distance node

* add nested acceptance

updates:
- adaptive distance node stores and evaluates all distance functions
- rejection sampler determines acceptance based on comparison between all distances and thresholds

note: removed adaptive rejection sampler

* add functional test

* allow user to continue iterative estimation

since adaptive distance SMC behaviour in each new round is determined based on previous populations, it is possible to let users continue iteration estimation.

* adaptive distance SMC without pool

this is an alternative implementation that does not use elfi output pool to store observations needed in distance adaptation but uses rejection sampler to handle adaptation.

* fix first iteration threshold

adaptive distance SMC did not work when batch size is smaller than the requested sample size because rejection sampler would generate the batch size rather than requested sample size when called with an infinite threshold.

* add consistency test

* fix stored statistics calculation

the adaptive distance node uses observed summaries data to calculate statistics based on which standard deviation can be estimated. previous version assumed that the individual summaries are scalar and did not work with vector summaries.

* add docstrings

* fix weighted distance calculation

* add unit tests

- check that the scale in adaptive distance node is calculated based on all data added between updates
- check that the distances in adaptive distance node correspond to euclidean distance between scaled summaries

* revise standard deviation update

previous version calculated standard deviation based on running totals that allowed incremental update but could lead to overflow problems.

* fix adaptive distance initialisation

* fix style issues

* fix docstrings style

* update changelog

* update method name

* fix nested acceptance

about nested acceptance: rejection sampler sorts samples based on distance and assumes that the n_samples first samples are the accepted sample. however when several distance functions and and thresholds are used as acceptance criterion, the smallest samples selected based on any one distance measure could contain samples that are not acceptable based on another distance measure and associated threshold.

about what was fixed: previous version checked whether a new batch contains samples where one or more distance measure is not below threshold and substituted all distances in such samples with infinities. this would ensure that the samples would not be sorted as smallest ones when the batch is merged with previous samples. however based on travis, the distances that were overwritten are a read-only variable in linux. hence this new version does not overwrite the distances but checks whether there are acceptable samples in a batch and if so, merges these with the previous samples.

* update docs

* update readme
